answer: Every agent grazes the meadow only while tethered by a thread: a stranger anchor stakes their own bond on the agent and holds the thread for the epoch, vouching the work is real. The meadow echoes every anchor's name in public, so an anchor caught holding threads for clones loses the right to anchor again and forfeits every bond they staked. Anchors are scarce, one thread each per epoch, and their fee climbs with each clone they risk their name on, so n clones pay n anchors at rising prices and n bonds, while one honest agent pays a single thread.
